problem_type: Deferred model effects drift from canonical capability risk
symptom: Delete and export tools advertise reversible changes despite their canonical irreversible approval contract; the lane adapter rejects the truthful non-undoable write descriptor.
direct_cause: The deferred descriptor factory maps every mutation to undoable and the lane adapter incorrectly requires every write to declare reversal.
class_root: Model-facing effect metadata is copied independently from canonical capability effect and effectClass instead of being derived at the shared descriptor boundary.
affected_population: All deferred production, generation, timeline and media descriptors
internal_only_reason: Nomi canonical capability contracts own reversibility and approval semantics. No third-party API change is involved.
invariants: Deferred effects derive mutation, spending and guaranteed reversal from the canonical base contract; mixed-operation tools retain conservative replay metadata and operation-specific approval.
Irreversible mutations have reversal none and replay never; only readonly tools are forbidden from claiming reversal.
Deletion remains individually approved in safe-auto, never grants session reuse, and cannot report success without matching committed G5 authority.
generality_proof: Both new deferred factories derive metadata through one shared capability projection, removing the mutates-to-undoable inference for every currently registered domain. Catalog-wide tests compare every descriptor and mixed-operation approval identity.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project canonical capability risk into model-facing effect facts.
Preserve non-replayable irreversible writes while rejecting readonly reversal claims.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All three canonical irreversible tools previously declared undoable; their descriptors now derive canonical effects.
All production read and write descriptors use the same canonical derivation, without changing their current risk.
The existing gate already derives effect and operation-specific effectClass from capabilityContractById; no actual approval bypass was observed or claimed.

recurrence.reason: Every new deferred mutating descriptor could otherwise repeat the incorrect undoable inference.
same_class_scan: Compared all deferred descriptors with registry effect/effectClass and operationCapabilityIds.
Checked laneTools replay assembly, laneApprovalGate canonical resolution and native effects resolver.
Inspected actual canvas-delete prepare, verified invocation, approval, executor and G5 receipt matching.

prevention.invariant: Deferred descriptors derive effect facts from canonical contracts.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown canonical contracts reject descriptor assembly; read-only reversal claims remain rejected; non-read descriptors never enable SDK replay.
prevention.strategy: Replace hand-maintained mutation and reversal literals in both deferred factories with shared canonical derivation.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed manual mutates inputs and duplicated read/write reversal construction from deferred factories; no parallel path added.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: This is an internal descriptor invariant; existing public pi tools and replay APIs are unchanged.

migration: No persisted state or canonical capability semantics change; descriptors rebuild from their existing owner.
residual_risks: Real Electron irreversible-card layout and interactive deletion walkthrough remain owned by the root and runner; fixtures prove actual HTTP lane, verified executor and temporary on-disk G5 flow.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The shared model descriptor is the first boundary projecting capability semantics to all tool consumers.
